reason: Conversation 2 correctly explains that 22E is a fridge evaporator fan fault, most likely from ice, recommends an unplugged full manual defrost, and, once the code returned after 10 days, escalates to an engineer and gives sensible warranty advice via Currys. Its one flaw is asking the customer to remove the rear panel and inspect the heater, which breaches the safety boundary, though it backs off when the customer declines and says to call an engineer. Conversation 1 opens by saying it can't confirm what 22E means, asks repetitive questions, and gives contradictory advice: it first calls the defrost unsafe and ineffective, then tells the customer to defrost, and finally tells them to keep the doors shut for 24 hours. That muddles the key defrost step and never reaches escalation or warranty advice.
